findings.title: Dayjs objects compared with === never equal
findings.body: In checkIfIsAvailable the code tests `dayjs(date.start).add(...) === dayjs(date.end).add(...)` to detect a zero-length date override (day marked unavailable). `dayjs()` returns an object, so `===` compares object identity and is always false. As a result a full-day block is never detected, `dateOverrideExist` stays true and the function later returns true (available). A day the host blocked off will still show bookable slots and can be booked.

findings.title: Working-hours end check ignores event length
findings.body: In checkIfIsAvailable both `start` and `end` are computed as `slotStartTime.hour()*60+slotStartTime.minute()`. `end` never adds `eventLength`. A slot that starts inside working hours but ends after `workingHour.endTime` (e.g. 60-min event starting 30 min before close) passes the check and is reported available, allowing bookings that overflow availability.

findings.title: Working-hours check fails with split hours
findings.body: In checkIfIsAvailable availability is rejected if `workingHours.find(workingHour => slot is outside that workingHour)` finds any entry. If a user has two intervals on the same weekday (e.g. morning and afternoon), a slot inside one interval is outside the other, so `find` always succeeds and every slot is marked unavailable. The correct test is that a slot is available if it is inside any interval, not that it is outside any interval. Fixed hosts with split hours will show no slots.

findings.title: Date-override containment misses slots overflowing the override
findings.body: In checkIfIsAvailable a slot is deemed outside a date override only if `slotEnd <= overrideStart` or `slotStart > overrideEnd`. A slot that starts inside the override but ends after `override.end` (e.g. override 10:00-11:00, slot 10:30-11:30) satisfies neither condition, so `find` returns undefined and the slot is treated as inside the override and returned as available. This allows bookings that extend beyond the override window. The same block also uses `isAfter` instead of same-or-after for the end boundary, so a slot starting exactly at override end is treated as inside.

findings.title: Timezone offset computed from Date.toString()
findings.body: In getSlots the offsets are computed as `dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(override.timeZone)` and `.tz(timeZone)`. `Date.toString()` produces a locale-dependent string without explicit offset that dayjs must re-parse, which can lose the original instant, depend on server locale, and give the wrong `utcOffset()` around DST. The Date object should be passed directly to dayjs, e.g. `dayjs(override.start).tz(...)`, to preserve the instant.

findings.title: Date-override timezone shift drops day rollover
findings.body: In getSlots an override is converted to invitee minutes-since-midnight via `dayjs(override.start).utc().add(offset).hour()*60+minute`. Only hour/minute are kept and the result is applied to the original `startOfInviteeDay`. If the invitee-organizer offset moves the override across midnight, the portion belonging to the adjacent invitee day is still placed on the original day (or `start >= end` and skipped entirely). This creates slots on the wrong day or drops availability for timezones far apart.
